A steel arch railway bridge over the gorge of the Chenab river in Reasi district of Jammu and Kashmir, India. Its deck stands about 359 metres above the river, higher than the Eiffel Tower, making it the highest railway bridge in the world. It opened in June 2025.

The bridge is part of a long railway line from Udhampur through the mountains to Srinagar and Baramulla, one of the hardest railway projects ever undertaken, with long tunnels through young, unstable Himalayan rock. Building began in the early 2000s and was slowed by safety redesigns, landslides and the remote site. The arch spans about 467 metres and was built to withstand very strong winds and earthquakes.

Its completion gave the Kashmir valley its first direct rail link to the rest of India. Prime Minister Narendra Modi opened it along with the first through trains to Srinagar. It continues the story of mountain railways in India that began with lines such as the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, in a region at the centre of the Kashmir conflict.
